transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Ever since all the changes at work, I feel like I’m reacting badly to everything and I can’t adjust to the new setup no matter how hard I try. I ended up getting a referral through my company's employee assistance program because I'm just having so much trouble coping with it all.
In addition to stress at work, have you been feeling down most of the day, nearly every day, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

I wouldn't say I feel down or depressed in a typical way, but I am so overwhelmed and on edge that I've completely stopped doing the things I usually enjoy. I've dropped my rec league basketball and museum visits because my life right now just revolves around stressing about work. The stress has completely taken over all my free time.
Do you often feel sudden waves of intense fear or discomfort that peak within minutes, such as heart racing, sweating, or feeling like you're choking or can't breathe?

No, I don't really get those physical feelings like my heart racing or having trouble breathing. While I definitely feel panicked or overwhelmed when sudden work changes happen, it doesn't turn into a physical attack like that. It's more of a mental overload where I just feel incredibly on edge.
How long have you been feeling this way, and do these feelings of being overwhelmed happen all the time or mainly in response to specific stressors at work?

These feelings have been going on for about four months now, starting a few weeks after the merger and restructuring took hold. They don't just happen out of nowhere; they are definitely tied to specific work stressors like last-minute schedule changes, shipping errors, and struggling with the new software.
